sentences.text: Scythosuchus was a heavy-built animal that grew to between 2 and 3 meters in length.
Fossils of this creature were discovered in Lower Triassic rock layers in Russia.
The name Scythosuchus translates to 'Scythian crocodile'.
The genus was formally described by Sennikov in 1999.
Scythosuchus basileus remains the only known species within this genus.
Scythosuchus possessed blade-like, serrated teeth with a backward curve adapted for slicing flesh.
This dental structure indicates that the animal was a carnivore.
The thick lower jaw with expanded articular areas suggests it had a powerful bite.
The cervical vertebrae had low, poorly developed neural spines with thickened tips that made the neck top-heavy.
Moving down the spine, the neural spines became thicker, heavier, and more rugose, resembling osteoderms.
The femur is well known from multiple specimens and has a sigmoidal shape with weak lateral compression.
It is classified as an extinct genus of rauisuchid.
This places the animal within the family Rauisuchidae.
Its parent group is identified as Vjushkovisaurini.
Sennikov (2022) proposed that Scythosuchus might be synonymous with Tsylmosuchus donensis.
However, Ezcuraa et al. (2023) reclassified Tsylmosuchus as a proterosuchid rather than a pseudosuchian, countering the synonymy hypothesis.
